Plan and usage are adjacent, with seat count, progress bar, consequence sentence and next-plan callout (app.js:429-496).
Copy consistently avoids claiming a successful payment and labels amounts as estimates (analysis.md:168-208).

The mobile prototype-controls bar clips the Data scenario select and truncates its label (inputs/condition-b/screenshots/mobile.png, top), making the scenario control hard to read.
An over-limit downgrade is a dead end: confirmation is disabled with an instruction to remove members, but no member-management route exists (analysis.md:179; app.js:927-968).
Plan and cancellation changes commit immediately with no busy/disabled state (app.js:974-1001, :1107-1118), leaving the brief's loading/commit feedback incomplete for consequential actions.
strengths: The single summary answers plan, price, renewal and member usage above the fold, with a plain consequence sentence at 80% usage (app.js:429-528).
Price display is explicitly separated from commitment: the monthly/annual toggle changes comparison prices only, with copy stating the subscription is unchanged (app.js:530-559).
Plan review states plan, member-limit delta, effective date, due today, next payment and payment method, and blocks an over-limit downgrade before commitment (app.js:888-972).
Coherent warm-grey and deep-green visual system that reads as a reliable account document, with one focal price and restrained status colour (screenshots/desktop.png; analysis.md:141-143).
Owner-only actions are replaced in place with explanations for members while retaining all read-only plan, usage, card and invoice data (app.js:354-366, :458, :582-591).

comparison: Both packets provide equivalent evidence: analysis, source, 1280px desktop and 390px mobile screenshots, and axe/DOM checks. Candidate A has the deeper interaction model and recovery coverage — loading/error/past-due/scheduled states, gated cancellation, validated card update with provider-failure handling, and busy states — plus fewer axe failures, but its prototype overlay obscures content and its cancellation seat policy is an unvalidated assumption. Candidate B has the stronger visual composition, always-visible plan comparison and the sharper judgment of separating price display from a billing change, but it carries serious contrast failures in both viewports, a dead-end over-limit downgrade and no in-flight confirmation feedback. Candidate A is ahead on the seven-dimension rubric.
limitations: One judge pass only; no statistical or causal claim. Screenshots cover the default owner state, so dialog, loading, error, member and scheduled-change visuals were inspected in source but not scored visually. Neither packet includes the claimed 36-/71-check interaction logs; test-output/checks.json contains only axe and DOM metrics. There was no screen-reader, manual keyboard, real payment-provider or real-browser matrix testing, and visual review is limited to the supplied 1280px and 390px full-page captures. All prices, proration, over-limit and cancellation policies are candidate assumptions and cannot be validated from the packets.
